newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine govt plans group to oversee c.bank - media.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine govt plans group to oversee c.bank - media.

text.p: Ukraine's Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko plans to head a special commission to oversee central bank activities, the national news agency DINAU reported on Friday.
The move comes after several weeks of government criticism of central bank activities in the former Soviet republic.

Lazarenko, who has been rapidly gaining power since his May appointment by President Leonid Kuchma, has specifically criticised the bank for not supporting the industrial sector in the former Soviet republic.

"The banking system here is closed off and has no desire to allow those with money into Ukraine, and it has led to this situation," Lazarenko was quoted as saying at a recent meeting with senior industry officials.
"If we don't solve these questions the government's goals will not be fulfilled," he said.
Lazarenko's three-year economic plan presented in September called for increased government support for producers, to boost Ukraine's flagging industrial sector.

The government has already prepared a document stating it will form the commission together with parliament, but the DINAU report did not say precisely what function the commission would perform or how wide-ranging its powers would be.
But a central bank official, who asked not to be identified, said the move would be illegal under Ukraine's constitution.
"Parliament reviews our performance and the president appoints the governor," he said. "The government likes to say this from time to time. Central bank independence is an irritating factor."
Bank Chairman Viktor Yushchenko led the introduction of Ukraine's new hryvnia currency in September, and Kuchma has said he does not intend to replace him.
